newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - EBRD, HSBC in Czech bank's revival plans.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - EBRD, HSBC in Czech bank's revival plans.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is considering acquiring up to 20 percent of troubled Agrobanka a.s. as part of the fifth largest Czech bank's restructuring.

Agrobanka's central bank-appointed administrator said the EBRD "had confirmed an interest" in taking a stake of "up to 20 percent", but EBRD participation would be separate from a majority holding to be sold to a strategic investor.
The Czech National Bank's (CNB) administrator, Jiri Klumpar, said the majority owner would hold a 51 percent stake in the bank, which suffered a liquidity crunch in September.
Klumpar said London's HSBC Investment Bank 0005.PR was chosen in a tender to advise on Agrobanka's reorganisation and conduct the selection of new investors in the next five months.

"The task of the financial adviser is the evaluation of the financial situation of the bank, its situation on the interbank market...and a proposal for the optimum restructuralisation structure of the basic capital of the bank," Klumpar said.
HSBC would also conduct "the negotiation with current shareholders and potential investors, finishing with the entry of one or several strategic investors into the bank," he added.
One criteria for the majority shareholder would be experience in managing a retail banking strategy.

The central bank put Agrobanka under what it called "temporary forced administration" in Septemeber because of its poor liquidity stemming from a loss of confidence on the Prague inter-bank money market.

The CNB said the crisis of confidence was due to Agrobanka's connection to a secretive Czech investment group called Motoinvest, and that it would search for a strategic equity partner to replace shareholders connected to Motoinvest.

The crisis came after the August failure of a small Plzen-based bank, Kreditni Banka a.s., which also was connected to Motoinvest. The exact stakes held by Motoinvest or investors connected to the group, have not been disclosed.
The majority stake would either come from a direct sale of shares culled from existing shareholders or an equity increase to achieve the 51 percent holding.
Agrobanka was the 12th bank to fall under administration of the CNB since post-Communist reforms began in the early 1990s, permitting the creation of nearly 60 banks.
Several of the troubled banks have been shut or liquidated.

The failure of Kreditni, after a series of dubious debt swaps, and the subsequent liquidity crisis at Agrobanka, sent shockwaves through the government and the central bank, as the situation became a political football.

The cabinet and the parliament have both established special bodies to investigate the crisis, and the central bank has recently set up a state-sponsored plan to buy back non-performing loans at 13 small private Czech banks.
More than 70 percent of Czech banking activity takes place with the four largest domestic banks.
